reviews.comment: I was honestly nervous when I saw Dr. Daniel had such a low score. It's surprising because the man is a wonderful professor. I had the honor of being his student for the last semester of his career, and I can confidently say that Texas A&M is losing one of their best. He is passionate, he is witty, and he genuinely cares. A great guy. 12/10
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Inspirational--Respected

reviews.comment: Professor Daniel is one of the best professors that I have taken at Texas A&M. He is retiring so this review won't matter in the future but I feel that the bad reviews are undeserved. Essays are short, while there are several of them, and showing up to class is enough to get a good grade. Did the minimum required and still made a B.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: My favorite professor at A&M. It's not an easy class for sure, but you get a lot out of it if you do the readings and prepare for the quizzes. Some people think he's rude, but if you're having trouble with the class, go to his office hours and he'll genuinely help you out. If you like a challenge/learning about Early Modern, I recommend highly.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Near impossible 4 question quizzes after every class. Worth little but the points add up, if you don't make a lot of 100's you can't get an A in the class. You can give the right answer on tests but if u didn't word it how he wants then he takes points off. Laughed when asked if he would drop a quiz and asked if we ever had consequences growing up.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Only take this class if it is mandatory. Professor Daniel is an amazing teacher, but do not expect to get an A or even a B. He is incredibly helpful in office hours, and this class challenged me to be a better reader. But, the daily quizzes are extremely hard and the two exams are too. The possibility of an A is next to none.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is by far the worst professor I have ever had. His lectures consisted of half of the time calling out random names for attendance and the other half debating with students. Every time someone would ask a question he would argue it rather than directly answering the question. Most of your grade is based off of the into and exit quizzes. Avoid
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The best way to succeed in this class is to go to office hours. Thought he was a rude and inconsiderate at the beginning of class but when I went to office hours it was completely different he broke down the lectures before hand helped with the quizzes a lot. Is very opinionated which definitely tied into the essay we wrote.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: 2 daily in class canvas quizzes, but people would look at other's screens for the answers. Has website with previous quizzes to help you. one essay, two tests. Questions are always confusing- thought I was going to get a C then last minute got an A+ (96) because he changed the grading and it benefitted everyone but seemed to good to be true!
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He called random names for attendance each day and if you have 3+ absences you go down an entire letter grade. He spent class time debating with students rather than actually teaching the material but if you read the powerpoints and textbook and do good on the class quizzes youll get an A.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would not take him again. We were graded on 2 quizzes every class, a midterm, 250 word essay, and a final. The quizzes are worth 50% of your grade. He took attendance almost every class period and if you miss more that 3 your grade will drop a letter grade. He grades based on opinion, so if you disagree with what he thinks you will score poorly.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Daniel is really intelligent but does not need to be teaching an introductory class. His lectures are confusing and he talks down to his students like were stupid because we have not seen this stuff before. 2 quizzes EVERY class that account for so much of you grade and are really confusing. Don't take unless you like pulling your hair out.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lectures are confusing, doesn't really answer questions. Quiz and test questions are difficult to understand. You could lose a letter grade for being absent more than 3 times.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The only reason I got an A in this class is because I went to office hours. There are two, 2 question, quizzes a day over the reading/lecture material and in total the quizzes make up half of your total grade for the class. It's doable, but I wouldn't recommend it. The reading is super interesting, but the grading policy and lectures make you dread
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I cant tell you a single thing I learned in this class because all he did in the class was debate with the students rather than giving to a direct answer. He does two quizzes every class one in the beginning and one at the end. He gives you three minutes to answer two questions and each quiz was worth 1% of your grade. Crash Course helped
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I would never recommend anyone to take a class from Prof. Daniel. While he is knowledgeable, he is awful at passing on that knowledge as he is aggressive and does not answer questions. Literally told us to just "be smarter." His test questions/answer choices are complex run-on sentences, it's hard to discern the question much less a correct answer.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Daniel only gets a 2 because he is very knowledgeable about his topic. He is aggressive during class discussions, which does not make a nice place to learn and open up about your thoughts. Also he is VERY VERY bad with his feedback. Would intentionally misread your essays so he could give you the grade he wanted, not the grade you deserved.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: To me, Dr. Daniel is an amazing professor. Funny, sarcastic, and EXTREMELY knowledgeable; however, he can also be a little rude, he's kinda bad with technology, and he grades somewhat harshly (he knows the material super well, so he knows BS when he sees it). TAKING NOTES WILL SAVE YOUR LIFE. COVID online: 4 papers, a midterm, and a final
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Terrible Teacher, Grading is unclear, No clear instructions for his papers. Overall if any other Philosophy teacher is available then take them. By taking this class you are ensuring you will not enjoy Philosophy nor will you find yourself wanting to take a course from this teacher again.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader

reviews.comment: Sloppy course, no clear direction. Grades papers without any clear rubric. Don't take if you want to still have a full head of hair at the end of the semester
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Daniel is a true philosopher, in the worst way, and prides himself on being vague. No clear grading criteria, unclear guidelines, and basically no prompt for essays. That doesn't stop him from putting REAL constructive criticism like "what does this mean?" when it is explained in the next few lines. Thought I'd like PHIL but after this guy, NO
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: There are no clear grading criteria, other than what he thinks of your essay. He tells you to use sources like the internet encyclopedia of philosophy. If he disagrees with your source he will take points off. There is not a way to do well in this class. Too difficult for intro and left me with a bad taste in my mouth for philosophy.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Daniel isn't a bad person, but where he is truly lacking is in grading essays fairly. Every single critique on your paper will be something along the lines of "what does this mean?" even after you spent the entire paragraph explaining what that sentence means. He doesn't read the essays. He just takes points off for whatever reason.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Daniel is a great professor and is clearly passionate about philosophy. I wasn't prepared nor did I take it seriously enough, for the heavier reading and four quizzes a week that make up about half of your grade combined so I didn't do as well as I could've, but he sets the class up for you to succeed if you keep up with the work
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is really knowledgeable on the subject. I really enjoyed him as a teacher! His lectures kept me very entertained. Only had a midterm and final, one section of chapter questions, and daily preclass and post class quizzes that made up the majority of your grade. Class isn't too hard, but does require effort.
reviews.ratingTags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Daniel is very knowledgeable on the material that he teaches, but the material itself is pretty complex. Class is a mix of discussion and lecture, and grades consist of 4 tests, 4 assignments, and some quizzes. He grades pretty critically, but if you read and attend class and his office hours before the test, you should pull an A.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I thought it was going to be easy- it wasn't. At the beginning he made it seem like it was! He grades on very specific details and I failed almost every assignment. There was a lot of reading, but the class was ok. (it was at 8am hard to stay awake tbh) Maybe the material just went over my head, but ultimately I had to Q-drop. NOT AN EASY CLASS!
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: My easiest class of the semester. All you have to do is skim the assigned reading before class and take good notes during lecture. He calls on people each class to answer a question about the reading, but if you look at the material before class it's straight-forward. All quiz/test questions are given in advance and gone over during class.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Daniel is by far one of the hardest professors you will ever have, but his class is beyond rewarding. I would always look forward to going to class, because I knew our discussions would be in depth and incredibly interesting. He is a tough but reasonable grader. Take. Him.  If I had the chance to do the class over again, I undoubtedly would.

For the Spring 2011 semester there is a 200 word essay due every Thursday, prompt given in class and a 500 word essay due every other Sunday. The class is interesting but gets a little tedious beacause Daniel likes to word bash people's opinions-and always take the easier side of the argument. Take him if you want to think about philosophy.

Harsh and bias grader.  Grades are based on 2 papers throughout the whole semester and a midterm and final.  All of which are very hard and you will def. fail unless you live in his office during his office hours.  STAY AWAY.  Not an easy class or prof compared to the other PHIL profs on campus for Intro to PHIL. He does teach very good though =]

Homework (not mandatory) takes about an hour to do every night, but if you do it, you don't have to pass the exams to get an "A" in the course.  I got a 75 and a 60 on the exams, but did the homework and made an A.
